name: Third International Theory
summary: The Third International Theory, also called the Third Universal Theory, is Muammar Gaddafi's doctrine in The Green Book, offered as an alternative to capitalism and Marxism. It rejects parliaments, parties and referendums in favour of direct popular rule through congresses and committees, abolishes wage labour in favour of worker partnership, and holds that the national and social bond, not class, drives history. It combines Arab nationalism, Islam, anti-imperialism and traditional views of family and sex roles.
scope: The Green Book (1975-79, three parts) as the canonical text, with the Libyan Jamahiriya (1977-2011) as its main practice. It excludes later pan-African developments beyond a brief mention and other doctrines also called Third Position.

sources.usedFor: Practice: nationalisation, state trade, repression, foreign policy.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice. Meeting basic needs outside the market is a core aim.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The Green Book treats wage labour itself as the problem, saying better wages leave it unsolved, so a wage floor is neither a goal nor opposed.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Economic activity is to serve needs rather than profit, and the regime replaced private trade with state-run supermarkets.

public-ownership.rationale: Gaddafi nationalised oil and key sectors, though the Green Book says state ownership alone leaves workers as wage-earners.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Wealth beyond personal needs is said to belong to society, which implies heavy claims on the rich.

unions-good.rationale: Unions work inside the wage system the theory rejects, and the regime allowed no independent unions; adherents would not clearly endorse them.

property-fundamental.rationale: Only property for personal needs is protected; land is "the private property of none" and wealth beyond needs belongs to society.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice. Private profit-making enterprise is rejected.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice. Satisfying basic needs is the basis of freedom.

worker-ownership.rationale: "Partners, not wage-earners": enterprises are to be owned and run by those who work in them.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The regime ran extensive surveillance through revolutionary committees for security; the theory itself is silent.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice. A conservative Islamic-nationalist state.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; the regime restricted speech widely but not on this ground.

strong-leader.rationale: Rule by an individual is classed with party and class rule as dictatorship; power is to rest with the people.

state-harmful.rationale: The Green Book wants authority held directly by the people rather than a state apparatus, but does not call the state unnecessary.

limit-guns.rationale: The motto puts weapons in the hands of the people, so strict limits on ownership run against it.

empower-police-military.rationale: Armed people are meant to replace a separate professional force, though the regime itself built a strong security apparatus.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice. Islamic and family-centred social views.

decide-locally.rationale: Power starts in local Basic Popular Conferences; the people decide directly at the base.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no clear line.

traditional-family.rationale: The family is the basic social unit and mothers are to raise children at home.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice. Natural-law view of sex roles and family.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice. Family-centred, Islamic social outlook.

more-religion-public.rationale: Islam is the state religion and religion is a source of law, but clerical influence is limited.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The Green Book foresees Black peoples regaining prominence after slavery and colonialism.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Sex roles are presented as natural law, not social convention.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: People are said to feel at home in their inherited arts, language and heritage; the social bond is central.

gradual-change.rationale: The theory arose from a revolution and presents itself as a decisive break with existing systems.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed by the theory; policy toward migrants varied.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Anti-imperialist and non-aligned; suspicious of Western-led bodies, favouring regional unions.

free-trade.rationale: Anti-imperialist economics and abolition of private trade point away from free trade.

nation-first.rationale: Nationalism is the driving social force, though adherents also prize pan-Arab and pan-African unity.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Anti-imperialism treats Western intervention as domination.

open-borders.rationale: The nation is the key social unit and its cohesion is to be protected.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The Green Book and its commentary never address this issue, and adherents have no settled line.

revolution-justified.rationale: The theory came from a revolution, though the Green Book calls violent revolution undemocratic compared with fully popular authority.

experts-over-public.rationale: No one may act in place of the people; the people decide directly.

central-planning.rationale: State ownership is said not to solve the problem, though the regime ran a state-directed economy.

socialized-markets.rationale: Self-employment and partnership enterprises are accepted, with trade serving needs.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; land is private property of none but taxes are not discussed.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Heirs may keep using land they live on, but accumulated wealth beyond needs is disfavoured; not addressed directly.

basic-income.rationale: "Those who produce consume": income comes from one's own work or partnership.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice. Anti-imperialist economics.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The regime directed oil revenue and development through the state.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Each person is to own the home, vehicle and means for their own needs, without employing others.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Wage labour is abolished in favour of partners, and profit and money are expected to disappear once needs are met.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice. The regime restricted private banking.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: With wage labour abolished there is nothing to bargain over; authority rests in popular conferences, not recognised bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: "The party is a contemporary form of dictatorship."

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Rule by an individual or minority is rejected; Gaddafi overthrew the monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: Democracy, defined as supervision of the people by the people, is the theory's central aim, whatever its critics say of the practice.

direct-votes.rationale: Laws are to be made by Basic Popular Conferences, a direct assembly; plebiscites with yes/no answers are called a fraud.

workers-councils.rationale: People's Committees and Congresses replace parliaments, though they are of the whole people, not workers alone.

right-to-secede.rationale: Multinational states are said to break up as the social factor wins, but secession was not endorsed in practice.

natural-rulers.rationale: No minority, class or individual may rule; authority belongs to all the people.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Green Book allows that power struggles are armed and the regime itself came by coup, though it prefers peaceful popular correction.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice.

separate-church-state.rationale: Religion and custom are named as the natural source of law, and Islam is the state religion.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Law should rest on custom and religion rather than man-made constitutions.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Power and weapons are to rest with the people, not private firms.

military-superiority.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice. Regime built large arsenals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Nations rest on shared origin and destiny, multinational states are unstable, but minorities keep rights.

class-struggle-history.rationale: History is driven by the social (national) factor, not by class, against Marx.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Production is divided equally among its components and needs are met for all.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The Green Book and its commentary never address this issue, and adherents have no settled line.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice. Anti-colonial stance.

civilizational-union.rationale: The project rests on pan-Arab and later pan-African union, which are national and continental rather than religious or civilizational unions; support for union on shared religion is inferred from Part 3's ties between religion and nation.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Profit-seeking is rejected as exploitation and the social bond is primary.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The Green Book states that rights are equal but responsibilities are not, and the group bond takes priority.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The Green Book and its commentary never address this issue, and adherents have no settled line.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice. Heritage and stability are valued.

human-enhancement.rationale: The Green Book and its commentary never address this issue, and adherents have no settled line.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Direct rule by the people is the point; delegating to algorithms is inconsistent with it.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice. Security state.

restore-past-order.rationale: Law is an "eternal human heritage", yet the theory presents itself as a new order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The theory claims to be a definitive solution, not a pragmatic one.

direct-action.rationale: Authority is exercised in popular assemblies rather than elections and parliaments.

means-match-ends.rationale: Violent revolution is called undemocratic; a democratic society should be built democratically.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Basic needs are to be met independently of employment, and in the final stage money disappears, though "those who produce consume" governs distribution.

production-for-use.rationale: Economic activity should satisfy needs, not accumulate profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: "The recognition of profit is an acknowledgment of exploitation."

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Classes, like parties, are minorities, and a class in power reproduces the struggle for domination.

collective-farming.rationale: Land is used by those who work it and their heirs, without employing others, rather than collectivised.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Anti-imperialist worldview, though it rejects Marxism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice. Collective social and religious norms matter.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Minorities with their own social framework have inherent rights, and the group bond is primary.

conscription.rationale: The regime conscripted citizens, including women from 1984, in line with an armed people.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The theory prizes popular participation over exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Citizens are to rule directly, not be customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Satisfying material needs independent of anyone's control is the basis of freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; the press is to be run by popular committees.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice.

organic-representation.rationale: "No representation in lieu of the people": delegates of any kind are rejected in favour of direct congresses.

total-state.rationale: The theory claims power rests with the people, though the regime was far from limited.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not framed as decadence and rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Pan-Arab unity was sought, but the theory does not call for conquest.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Tribal loyalty is a social bond, but the regime curbed tribal leaders and authority is to be popular.

bound-labor.rationale: Land is private property of none and employing others on it is forbidden.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The Green Book and its commentary never address this issue, and adherents have no settled line.

universal-morality.rationale: The Green Book presents natural law as binding, though tied to each nation.

single-common-good.rationale: Parties and classes represent factions; the theory seeks a single popular will with no competing minorities.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Libya was hostile to Israel. The sources do not address this directly; the answer is inferred from its core principles.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The Green Book and its commentary never address this issue, and adherents have no settled line.

revive-national-language.rationale: Inherited language is held central to a nation's heritage.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workers are partners in running enterprises under the people's authority.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice. Education is a matter for the people, not markets.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The Green Book and its commentary never address this issue, and adherents have no settled line.

economic-freedom.rationale: The Green Book ties political freedom to economic emancipation of people from employers.

rule-by-example.rationale: The Green Book and its commentary never address this issue, and adherents have no settled line.

national-self-determination.rationale: Each nation is a natural social unit and multinational states are expected to break up.

force-without-un.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice. Hostile to Western-led bodies.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Religion and custom are sources of law and Islam is the state religion.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The Green Book and its commentary never address this issue, and adherents have no settled line.

class-collaboration.rationale: Workers are partners rather than wage-earners and class struggle is not the driver of history.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inherited culture, arts and language are valued.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-imperialism and non-alignment are central; Gaddafi promoted a Third World alternative to both blocs.

workers-nation.rationale: The social factor is national, not class-international.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Men and women are equal as humans but have different natural roles; women should not do men's work.

ban-interest.rationale: Profit is called exploitation, and the state religion is Islam; interest is not addressed directly.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice. Pan-African outlook.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Party, class or tribe rule is described as minority domination.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Libya's economy depended on oil, but the theory is silent.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The Green Book and its commentary never address this issue, and adherents have no settled line.

proportional-representation.rationale: Parliaments and parties are rejected outright.

national-mission.rationale: The Third Universal Theory is offered as a model for Third World countries, not for export by force.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Gender differences are called natural, not systematic male advantage.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Parliaments misrepresent the people and parties serve minorities.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice. The regime used its forces without such accountability.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The theory demands broad economic and social transformation.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice. Pan-African outlook.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Men and women are equal as human beings, though with unequal duties.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice. The theory looks to pan-Arab and pan-African unity.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Libya opposed Israel and colonialism. The sources do not address this directly; the answer is inferred from its core principles.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice. Religion and custom ground law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The Green Book and its commentary never address this issue, and adherents have no settled line.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice. Islam is the state religion.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The theory puts power in the people, not a strengthened state.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Democracy is supervision of the people by the people.

trade-surplus.rationale: The Green Book and its commentary never address this issue, and adherents have no settled line.

population-transfer.rationale: Minorities are said to have inherent rights.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice. The regime used force abroad.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: History is said to move through struggle between national groups.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: All parties are banned as dictatorship.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Dependence on an employer is called a form of slavery whether or not abused.

separated-powers.rationale: Authority is to be concentrated in the popular congresses.

vanguard-party.rationale: Party rule is a form of dictatorship and the people must rule directly.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice. Satisfying everyone's needs.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Rent is abolished and tenants become owners of their homes. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The Green Book and its commentary never address this issue, and adherents have no settled line.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Multinational states are held to fall apart as the social bond triumphs.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The regime suspended protections to fight opponents; the theory is silent.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The regime ran state supermarkets for essentials; basic needs are not to be left to the market.

party-controls-media.rationale: The press is to be run by popular committees, not owned by a party or private groups, though the regime censored heavily.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party rule is rejected and the people are to hold arms.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The Green Book and its commentary never address this issue, and adherents have no settled line.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The theory rejects delegates and elite privilege.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Parties are a form of dictatorship and rejected.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Pan-Arab and later pan-African union were central aims.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Rule by one person is classed as dictatorship.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed; clerical authority is limited.

clerical-rule.rationale: Clerical influence was limited and Salafists were imprisoned.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its principles and the Jamahiriya's practice. Conservative social values.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed; the theory rejects personalised rule.

recall-officials.rationale: Committees are supervised by the popular conferences.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The regime expelled foreign bases and stressed non-alignment.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Renting housing, even from the state, is held to compromise freedom; tenants became owners.

people-in-arms.rationale: The motto puts "power, wealth and weapons" in the hands of the people.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Inferred from the Green Book's praise of tribal and nomadic life and its idea that land belongs to no one and is worked by those who use it.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Arab unity was central to Gaddafi's politics, and the Green Book makes the nation the basic unit of history, so a divided people should be one state.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Green Book's distrust of representatives and experts against the direct rule of ordinary people.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Inferred from Part 3's view that each nation has its own culture and heritage; Gaddafi also stressed Arab-Islamic distinctiveness, so this is not firm.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its law from custom and religion and from the Jamahiriya's harsh practice.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from the Green Book's distinct sex roles and Islamic-traditional family values, which sit badly with school teaching of gender equality.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Green Book's religious basis for law and the Islamic character of the state.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Islamic and traditional social order the doctrine upholds.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred from the Green Book's view of the nation as a blood and cultural bond, which favours descent over birth on the soil.

minority-language-support.rationale: Part 3 says each people has the right to its own language and culture, but the Jamahiriya suppressed Amazigh, so doctrine and practice conflict.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; the state was Islamic and law came from religion, while the doctrine also recognises minorities' rights.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred from the Green Book's emphasis on tradition, family and the social bond over individual self-expression.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the doctrine's anti-imperialism and its view of exploitation by foreign capital.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Green Book says true freedom needs economic liberation, abolishing wage labour, rent and profit, not just national or political change.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred: it rejects parliaments and rules by popular congresses, which a new people-made order implies, though the Jamahiriya was declared by the leadership.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Adherents are split: the Jamahiriya suppressed political freedoms in practice, but the Green Book presents itself as the ultimate democracy.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from its anti-imperialist, Third World solidarity; Libya funded aid and liberation movements, though the text sets no duty.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; the doctrine favours an armed people and independence from blocs, but Libya's weapons programme was abandoned in 2003.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The Green Book rejects representation and elections of any kind as a false democracy, so a directly elected president is opposed.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Inferred: money and wealth are to be controlled by the people and the state, so an independent bank pursuing price stability is unlikely to be endorsed.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred from its Arab nationalism and anti-Zionism, which refuse to concede Palestine for settlement.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Part 2 holds that land belongs to no one and that ownership is limited to satisfying personal needs, without exploiting others.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Green Book holds that state ownership leaves workers as wage earners, which Gaddafi condemned; Marxist states are not accepted as true socialism.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; no clear principle points either way, so inferred indifference.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred from Gaddafi's anti-imperialism and rejection of foreign alliances and bases; the Jamahiriya opposed Western-led blocs, though it favoured Arab and African unity.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism and the Palestinian cause: territory taken by force from a people is illegitimate, though the Green Book does not state this.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Inferred: the Jamahiriya subordinated religion to the state's reading of Islam and rejected clerical authority, but the doctrine is itself Islamic and the Green Book does not address church property.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred: the Green Book rejects representation and the Jamahiriya formally had no head of state, with Gaddafi acting as "Guide" of the revolution, a partisan revolutionary leader rather than a neutral symbol.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from the nation-and-social-bond doctrine and the regime's practice of suppressing internal revolt; not stated in the Green Book.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred from the Green Book's stress on local popular congresses and the nationalities' social bond, though the Jamahiriya itself was highly centralised.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The Green Book rests authority on the people and condemns individual rule, and the regime was republican and officially Islamic, with no divine-descent claim for its leader.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine abolishes wage labour and favours equality of economic partnership, so a flat tax sits uneasily, though it does not discuss taxation.

character-from-environment.rationale: Part 3 and the Green Book's economics treat people as shaped by social conditions and call for changing them, though it also stresses innate sex differences.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Green Book holds that law should be grounded in custom and the Quran and be made by the people through congresses, not by an individual ruler standing above it.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; the Jamahiriya funded some technical projects, but nothing in the doctrine makes space a goal, so inferred indifference.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The Green Book rejects mixed or representative constitutions in favour of direct popular rule; inferred from Part 1's critique of every other system.

leader-cult.rationale: Green Book Part 1 classes rule by an individual as dictatorship and puts authority in the people's congresses, so glorifying a leader as the nation's embodiment goes against the stated theory, though Libyan practice did the opposite.

equal-parenting.rationale: Inferred from Part 3's traditional view of sex roles, in which women's and children's ties differ; the doctrine says nothing on custody.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The Green Book rejects class struggle as the engine of history and says the national and social bond decides it, though it also says a class win would end in the victory of one class.

land-redistribution.rationale: The Green Book says land is no one's property and may be used only by those who work it themselves, without employing others.

refugee-return.rationale: Gaddafi's Libya backed the Palestinian right of return and Arab national causes; inferred, not in the Green Book.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Gaddafi pursued Arab unity schemes and the Aouzou Strip claim, but the Green Book speaks of nations, not state territory claims; split.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Gaddafi grounded the Jamahiriya in Islam and sharia as the law of society, but his own interpretation was heterodox and the Green Book does not prescribe penalties for apostasy.

women-must-cover.rationale: The Green Book stresses women's distinct nature but does not call for compulsory coverings, and Gaddafi's Libya did not require them.

common-currency.rationale: Gaddafi promoted Arab and African unity, including a gold dinar for Africa; inferred from this.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The Third International Theory rests on the national bond, and Gaddafi pushed Arab and later African political unions across borders. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The Green Book makes the nation the unit of social life and has no concept of minority self-government; inferred from the national emphasis.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The Green Book holds that national liberation justifies a people having its own homeland; inferred, not addressed directly.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Part 3 argues that the social, national factor is the engine of history and rejects the Marxist account that economics alone decides it.

ban-cartels.rationale: The Green Book abolishes private enterprise and wage labor altogether, so competition policy is not at issue; split.

no-bailouts.rationale: The Green Book says nothing about bailouts; the Jamahiriya state owned the economy directly.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The Green Book says the people's congresses are the only legitimate legislators and law is based on custom and religion, not judge-made limits on popular rule.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The Green Book argues that men and women have distinct natural roles, so it does not call for equal representation quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The Green Book stresses producers owning what they produce and a self-reliant economy, but it does not demand autarky; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; no clear inference.

moral-incentives.rationale: The Green Book treats work for wages as a form of slavery and replaces it with partnership, but it grounds this in satisfying material needs, not moral incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The Green Book does not address revolutionary strategy; the 1969 officers' coup and Libyan backing of armed movements point one way, while the theory's demand for direct popular authority points the other.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Gaddafi overthrew the Libyan monarchy and the Green Book rejects exploitation and inherited power, though it honors the tribe as a social bond.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Part 3 makes the national bond the driver of history, from which a nation-centred history is inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The theory is anti-imperialist and holds that every people should rule itself.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred from the Green Book's emphasis on nationalism and the national bond.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book's terms; inferred indifference to preferences in admissions and hiring.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred from the abolition of private profit and the Jamahiriya's state control of banking and trade.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Inferred from the Green Book's view that the wage system must be abolished; it does not predict collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from its anti-imperialism; it seeks Arab and African unity rather than influence modelled on an imperial predecessor.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred from its anti-imperialist economics and the Jamahiriya's state-controlled trade.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The Green Book treats all wage workers as wage slaves and speaks of partners, not a privileged rich-country working class.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred from the Green Book's rejection of private ownership beyond personal needs; owners have no right to exclude.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Part 1 rejects constitutions as a basis of rule, placing law in custom and religion rather than a written charter.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from the theory's anti-imperialism and Arab-unity aims; the Green Book does not discuss colonial treaties.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Green Book calls elections and representation a fraud and has the people rule directly, so it rejects election of rulers as well as inheritance.

minority-veto.rationale: Part 1 attacks majority rule as the dictatorship of a bare majority over a minority, a concern inferred to favour minority consent.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from popular sovereignty: authority belongs to the people's congresses, which may remove their committees.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Part 1 rejects parliaments as a misrepresentation of the people and replaces them with popular congresses.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Islamic and traditional ethics the theory draws on, which counsel kindness to animals.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Islamic framing in which animals may be used for food with humane treatment.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The theory abolishes rent, wages and class privilege in favour of partnership and satisfied needs, not paternal duty from the privileged.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Direct democracy requires every citizen to take part in basic popular congresses, so withdrawal is rejected.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Part 1 treats the press and parliaments as tools of dominant interests; inferred sympathy with the claim.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Part 1 argues parliaments and parties secure acceptance of rule by sham representation; inferred from that argument.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred from its anti-imperialist, anti-capitalist stance and Libya's third-world positioning.

native-born-offices.rationale: Part 3 treats the nation as the basis of social life; inferred preference for natives, not stated as an office rule.

party-own-road.rationale: The theory presents itself as a distinct path rejecting both Marxism and capitalism and any foreign model.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from the Green Book's stress on producing for one's own needs and ending dependence on others.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from Libya's irredentist claims, such as the Aouzou Strip, under Gaddafi.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from Gaddafi's anti-settler stance, including the 1970 expulsion of Italians; contested given his Arabization policies.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The theory rejects constitutions in favour of the Quran and popular congresses, so it would not make any -ism a constitutional founding value.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: It condemns capitalism and Marxism as failed systems but does not frame them under a totalitarianism concept.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Part 3 discusses black slavery as a historical wrong; inferred that adherents see it as central to the conflict.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from the Jamahiriya's removal of colonial and monarchist symbols.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Part 3 stresses natural role differences and women's oppression; inferred not to favour equal programmes.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from Part 3's view of women as the oppressed party and fixed sex roles.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The theory offers its own solution to democracy for Arab-Islamic society and rejects Western parliamentary forms.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The Green Book wants the people armed rather than a separate military power, though Gaddafi came to power by an army coup.

paid-care-work.rationale: Part 3 treats domestic and maternal roles as natural to women, and Part 2 rejects wage labour.

filial-duty.rationale: The Green Book treats the family as the basic social unit and upholds traditional roles; filial duty is inferred from that and Islamic norms.

office-by-exam.rationale: The Green Book rejects representative and elite rule in favour of popular congresses and committees; examination-selected officials contradict direct popular rule.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its economic nationalism and rejection of private ownership of the means of production.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The Green Book is traditional on family and sex roles but does not address divorce; inferred and split.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The Green Book calls for popular congresses and committees to decide directly and rejects representation, with leaders accountable to the congresses.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The Green Book says people are partners not wage earners and rejects private ownership beyond personal need, and the Jamahiriya ran social security as a state function. The sources do not address this directly; the answer is inferred from its core principles.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The Green Book states land belongs to no one and a person may use it only to meet their own needs without hiring others.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Green Book calls parliaments a falsification of democracy and rejects them in favour of direct popular rule.

single-official-language.rationale: The Green Book treats language as bound up with national culture and Arabic prevailed in the Jamahiriya, but it did not deal with this issue; Amazigh suppression suggests agreement.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Green Book's strong principle that land is not private property and from nationalism.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The Green Book views class and nation as the drivers of history and treats racial inequity as secondary; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The Green Book condemns needs being met by markets and luxury, and holds that satisfying needs, not accumulation, is proper; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The Libyan Jamahiriya funded and armed foreign insurgent groups, including the IRA and others, as anti-imperial policy.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Gaddafi opposed foreign interventions, with Libya's anti-imperialist stance applying to great powers such as the USSR as well; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: The Green Book argues that parliaments and parties represent the dominant class or interests rather than the people; inferred to extend to corporate influence.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The doctrine is strongly anti-imperialist and defends national self-determination; inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The Green Book Part 3 upholds the family and traditional roles for the nation's continuity; inferred as favouring pronatalism.

residents-only-property.rationale: Part 2 says a house must belong to its occupant and not be rented, so ownership follows residence; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: Part 2 abolishes wage labour and makes everyone a producer partner; inferred as a right to work.

democratic-peace.rationale: Part 1 rejects representative democracy as false democracy; inferred that it would not credit democracies with peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The Green Book holds that law must derive from custom and religion, not from rulers or parliaments; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Anti-imperialism and national self-determination imply opposing outside intervention; inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: Part 2 organises production in workplace committees of partners, which is neither craft nor industrial unions as such.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not a doctrine of the Green Book; inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Part 3 on the family and women upholds the natural family and traditional roles.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Rule by popular congresses implies open information; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Part 2's emphasis on self-satisfaction of needs implies local self-sufficiency; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: The popular congresses and committees are formal structures; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The doctrine stresses national sovereignty and anti-imperialism; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Part 3 treats religion and nationalism as the two bonds of society, so adherents combine the two; no source defines the nation by religion alone.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from the Green Book's anti-imperialism and the Jamahiriya's stress on national independence, which reject submission to a great power.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred: the Green Book treats the nation's wealth as belonging to society as a whole, shared through popular congresses.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Part 2 says a person's house, vehicle and income to meet needs are private, while the means of production belong to society as partners.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred: Gaddafi rejected Marxism as a rival theory but dealt with the Soviet bloc and did not make defeating communism an aim.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred: the Green Book rejects profit-making and wage labour, so private providers within a public system do not fit.

religion-illusion.rationale: The theory makes Islam and the Quran a basis of society, and Part 3 treats religion as a lasting social bond.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Part 2 condemns wage labour and capital as exploitation and presents the theory as a replacement, not a continuation.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Part 3 treats the sexes as naturally different and does not tie women's position to the economic system.

socialized-care.rationale: Part 3 criticises nurseries and says children belong with their mothers in the family.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred from the regime's Arabization policies and Arab nationalism, which promoted Arabic over foreign languages.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred: the regime cancelled foreign treaties and bases and put popular sovereignty above inherited agreements.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: the Jamahiriya organised society into local people's congresses and committees, with workers as partners in production.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred: no settlement policy is documented in the sources, and the theory stresses the social bond of each nation rather than state steering of settlement.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The theory is presented explicitly as a third course beyond capitalism and Marxism, hence 'Third' International Theory.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Part 3 of the Green Book grounds the nation in shared history and culture, but it does not address land claims between peoples; treated as neutral.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Gaddafi was strongly anti-Zionist but the Green Book does not deny the Holocaust; inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The Green Book is silent, but Libya under Gaddafi kept the criminal ban and the doctrine appeals to Islam and traditional family; inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Green Book bans parties as instruments of dictatorship and the Jamahiriya banned and punished opposition groups, so this is closer to the doctrine's practice than to its text.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The doctrine treats Islam as part of the national bond and sharia as a source of law; the Green Book does not discuss blasphemy, so inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Third International Theory is explicitly anti-imperialist, opposing colonial domination of one nation by another.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Gaddafi backed anti-colonial resistance and presented Islam as part of the national struggle; the specific duty is not stated, so inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The Green Book makes the people's congresses the authority and treats religion as tradition, but it does not discuss forcibly removing rulers on religious grounds.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Part 1 argues that true democracy is direct popular rule through basic congresses and committees, rejecting representation by officials.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Part 3 holds that the national and social bond rather than class drives history, so class oppression is not treated as the lens that overlaps with others; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The Green Book's natural-role views on men and women and Libyan law under Gaddafi suggest rejection; inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: Traditional and Islamic outlook makes support for assisted dying unlikely; inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The Third Theory presents itself as a solution beyond both capitalism and Marxism, which is close to combining ideas of each; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Part 2 argues wage labourers are like slaves who do not own what they produce and calls for partners instead of wage earners.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Islam is part of the Third Theory's national and social base, so incompatibility claims would be rejected; inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Part 1 holds that authority belongs to the people exercised through congresses, though Part 3 gives religion weight as tradition.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The doctrine gives religion a role in social life and the Libyan state favoured Islamic dress norms; inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The Green Book wants workers protected from employer domination, but does not address NDAs; inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: Part 2 rejects both wage-based private markets and state ownership in favour of partnership, which differs from a social market economy.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Part 1 favours arming the people and the Jamahiriya kept large forces and conscription, so abolition is unlikely; inferred.

rich-first.rationale: Part 2's goal of equal satisfaction of needs and no exploitation of others rejects allowing some to grow rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Libya under Gaddafi pursued non-alignment and rejected both Cold War blocs; inferred from that practice.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The Green Book vests rule in the people through popular congresses and rejects representation, leaving no place for hereditary office.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred: the Green Book abolishes profit and the Jamahiriya nationalized banks, so credit is state-run rather than a user-owned mutual system.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's anti-imperialism and the Jamahiriya's rejection of Western economic control.

property-franchise.rationale: The Green Book makes every citizen a member of the popular congresses, and calls representation a fraud, so a property franchise contradicts it.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Part 3 holds that men and women have different natural roles, which cuts against a shared-domination view, though the Green Book also condemns oppression of women.

reification.rationale: Inferred from Part 2's claim that wage labour is a form of slavery that hides exploitation, though the Green Book does not use reification.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The Green Book argues that a press owned by an individual expresses only its owner and must be owned by society, so wealth cannot be allowed to control it.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Part 1 grounds law in unchanging custom and religion, not in rulers' decrees, but the Jamahiriya ruled by revolutionary decree.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Green Book makes the nation, not race, the social bond, but the Jamahiriya privileged Arab identity.

online-participation.rationale: Inferred: direct popular rule suits any means of participation, though the Green Book predates the internet.

open-government-data.rationale: The Green Book favours popular rule but the Jamahiriya practised secrecy; no source settles it.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Part 3 grounds law in religion and the Jamahiriya applied Islamic family law, which limits Muslim women from marrying outside the faith.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine treats minorities' rights as secured by the nation, and no boycott practice is recorded.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The Green Book has all citizens decide directly in popular congresses rather than a selected group; inferred from that, as lot-chosen assemblies are not its mechanism.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Gaddafi urged going back to the Quran over later clerical tradition, so a committed adherent would favour rethinking inherited rulings; inferred from his religious stance.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Green Book abolishes wage labour and private rent and gains and says wealth should not enable some to exploit others, which implies concentrations of wealth threaten freedom.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its traditional and Islamic views of sex roles and the Jamahiriya's conservative social practice.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Green Book treats religion as part of the tradition that sustains the nation and condemns atheism and its suppression by Marxism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The Green Book does not address policing, but the Jamahiriya used security forces and prisons extensively; it has no abolitionist element, though it speaks of the people's own enforcement of society's law.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The Green Book rejects representation and majority-minority party contests in favour of direct popular rule by all; guaranteed shares for communities is not discussed, so it is inferred and the answer leans against it.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The Green Book makes the satisfaction of basic needs (housing, income, transport) a right guaranteed by society, not left to charity or private discretion.

term-limits.rationale: Gaddafi held no formal office, and the Green Book rejects elected representatives altogether, so limits on elected terms are not addressed; inferred as neutral.

vote-delegation.rationale: The Green Book rejects representation and proxy as fraud and demands direct participation of each person in the people's congresses; delegation to others is the thing it opposes.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The Green Book does not address long-term catastrophic risk, and it is not clear what it implies.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The Green Book holds that men and women differ by nature and have distinct roles, and Jamahiriya religious practice followed Islamic norms; inferred and not stated directly for offices.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Green Book asserts women's equality as human beings but different natural roles; whether it extends to authority in marriage is not stated and the Jamahiriya mixed both.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from the Green Book's emphasis on the national bond as the unit of political life.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from Part 2's view that housing is a need that must not be exploited for profit; it goes further than capping.

abolish-ip.rationale: Part 2 limits private exploitation of wealth but does not address patents or copyright.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from the armed-people doctrine and the Jamahiriya's revolutionary youth and military training.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism and the call for the people to hold arms, not foreign powers.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Anti-imperialism is core, and Libya expelled British and US bases in 1970 (see the history of the Gaddafi period).

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from the anti-colonial stance; Libya pressed Italy for colonial-era reparations.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Part 2 rejects wage labour and calls workers partners who receive the product of their work.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from the armed-people doctrine, which makes defending the community by force a duty.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from Part 3's view that national bonds drive history.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Part 3 holds that man and woman differ by nature and assigns them different roles.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from Part 3's naturalised, fixed view of woman's role.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from the cult of anti-colonial resistance fighters in Libyan state ideology.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred from the Green Book's treatment of religion as a basis of social identity and a guide in the struggle against imperialism.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred from the pan-Arab aim of unifying the nation, not splitting it into centre and diaspora.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from the Jamahiriya's state-building programme of congresses and committees.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from the traditional religious and family views in the Green Book.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from Part 3's rejection of equating the roles of men and women.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from Part 3's stress on the national bond; minorities were not given separate status.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from the national-bond doctrine and the aim of Arab unity.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from the Jamahiriya's practice, where unions were folded into the popular committees and state structure rather than standing apart from them.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The Green Book makes workers partners rather than wage-earners and puts rule in popular committees, but frames power as belonging to the whole people, not the working class alone.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the Green Book's treatment of housing, health and basic needs as matters for society, and from the nationalisations and state services of the Jamahiriya.

second-chamber.rationale: The Green Book rejects parliaments outright as a misrepresentation of the people, so a second chamber beside an elected parliament has no place in it.

municipal-property.rationale: The Green Book places productive property with the producers as partners and with society as a whole, not with the local community as such.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from the structure of basic popular congresses feeding a General People's Congress, which coordinated their decisions; in practice the national level governed more than the statement allows.

family-wage.rationale: The Green Book abolishes wage labour in favour of partnership and meeting household needs, so it endorses the aim of supporting a family but not the wage form the statement names.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed by the Green Book; no position can be inferred from its principles.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed by the Green Book; no position can be inferred from its principles.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from a state-run economy that nationalised trade and banking and a regime that monitored and repressed dissent, which sit badly with untraceable money.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the Jamahiriya's surveillance and repression of dissent and its rule through popular committees that identified every participant.

person-over-state.rationale: The Green Book holds that the social bond of nation and family comes first and that true freedom lies in collective popular rule, not in the individual set against the community.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The Green Book makes religion and tradition a basic social factor alongside nationalism, and the theory is presented as grounded in Islam.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from the Green Book's view that sovereignty rests with the base congresses, so local authority is not a grant that a national legislature could withdraw.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed by the Green Book; the regime's agricultural self-sufficiency projects suggest no clear stance on genetic engineering.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed by the Green Book; no position can be inferred from its principles.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The Green Book treats race alongside nation as a historical factor and predicts the rise of the black and yellow races, so it accepts groups organising around such bonds; it rejects racism as such.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from the Green Book's stress on the pride and historical role of nations and peoples, and from Gaddafi's Arab and African nationalism.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The doctrine supports armed liberation movements and the Jamahiriya intervened abroad, for example in Chad, so it does not limit force to self-defence.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The Green Book makes the national bond, based on shared history and culture, a driver of history, and the doctrine is built on Arab nationalism across state borders.

communal-electorates.rationale: The Green Book rejects representation and parliaments; the people rule directly through congresses, so separate sectarian electorates are contrary to it.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's anti-imperialism and Gaddafi's pan-Arab outlook; not stated directly in the Green Book.

free-public-college.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its view that basic needs such as education are a right not to be sold, and the Jamahiriya offered free schooling.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not addressed; the Green Book is about ownership and rule, and the regime relied on oil revenue.

future-generations.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; no stated position on the environment.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Part 3 says men and women are equal as human beings but have natural differences in roles, and rejects treating women as men's equivalent in all functions rather than valuing a distinct political contribution.

arms-reduction.rationale: The doctrine favours an armed citizenry and the regime kept large arsenals; inferred from the people-in-arms principle.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from the Green Book's call for direct rule by the people and its criticism of closed rule, though Libyan practice was often secretive.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from the Jamahiriya's state control of the economy and oil, since Part 2 puts wealth under popular control; not discussed directly.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The Green Book envisions a society in which all the people share authority, wealth and arms, and the Jamahiriya armed the people, so a standing state monopoly is rejected.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The Green Book treats wars as struggles of nations and classes; no doctrine of conscientious refusal, but its rejection of professional armies in favour of the armed people implies it; inferred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The Green Book calls wage labour a form of slavery and expects trade unions to give way to partnership and syndicates, so wage bargaining is not the goal.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of the wage system, which tax credits to wage earners would preserve.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed by the Green Book.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Anti-imperialism and opposition to economic hegemony are central, inferred from the Third Universal Theory.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Part 1 rejects parliaments, parties and representation, and replaces the state with Popular Conferences and People's Committees.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The Green Book presents one fixed economic solution, partnership and abolition of wages, as universal, rather than open experiment.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The Green Book treats natural resources as the common property of the people to be used for need rather than priced; inferred.

sacred-nation.rationale: Part 3 calls the national bond the driving force of history, rooted in the nature of the human group, though sacredness is not stated.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed by the Green Book.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book, which treats colonialism as national oppression; internal regional exploitation is not discussed.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Part 3 grounds the family and the sexes in human nature, though it speaks of natural roles rather than rights and dignity; inferred.

public-service-media.rationale: Part 1 says the press must belong to society through People's Committees, not to private persons; it is non-commercial but not independent of popular authority.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Part 3 says each nation should have its own religion, so it is not framed as one truth behind all; inferred from that and Islamic commitments.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from Part 2: land belongs to none and farmers work it themselves, with the state protecting those who live from their labour.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; the Jamahiriya sought such weapons for years before disarming in 2003, so no stable position.

workers-own-party.rationale: Part 1 rejects parties as a form of dictatorship and wants direct popular rule through congresses, so no independent party of any class.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed by the Green Book; inferred from its traditional views of sex roles, with no clear position.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Part 3 holds there is no difference in human rights between man and woman and calls the woman owner of the house, but inheritance of land is not discussed.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Part 3 calls for one inherited language as a distant goal but does not discuss how regional names relate.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from Part 2: productive property is held by the people and workers as partners, not by owners facing private suits.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Part 1 vests law in the people's congresses and the constitution of society, with no role for chiefs, though Part 3 values tribal ties.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; no stated position.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not addressed; Part 1 puts law in the hands of the people, so sentencing is not a stated issue.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from Part 3's view that the national bond and shared language underpin social unity.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from Part 2, where workers become partners and a separate union bargaining against employers has no place; the Jamahiriya ran a single state federation.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from Part 1, which treats voting and representation as a fraud and puts rule in popular congresses.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the Jamahiriya's use of Islamic law as national law and its Sunni orientation.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Part 1 rejects elections, parliaments and representation as a sham and demands direct popular rule.

premarital-sex.rationale: Part 3 treats the family and tradition as the base of society, and Libya criminalized sex outside marriage.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the regime's record, including cutting internet access in the 2011 uprising.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from Part 2, which abolishes wage labour and treats paid-for dependency as slavery; a cash payment is a wage in another form.

women-suffrage.rationale: Part 3 says women and men are equal as human beings, and women sat in the Basic People's Congresses.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Part 3 takes religion and tradition as a pillar of the social bond and blames society's forced roles, not religion, for women's condition.

race-social-construct.rationale: Part 3 treats colour races as natural groupings with their own historical cycles, not as inventions.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from Part 3's view that the sexes have natural roles and from its rejection of specialized state machinery in favour of the people's committees.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Part 2 of the Green Book holds that land is nobody's property and that people may use it only for their own needs, which rejects owning land by first claim.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the Jamahiriya's anti-imperialist hostility to Western-led institutions; the Green Book does not discuss international courts.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The theory makes Islam and the Quran a basis of society, and the Jamahiriya declared the Quran its law, but the Green Book does not state a doctrine of literal inerrancy.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Part 3 treats women and men as equal humans with different natural roles, and the Jamahiriya promoted women's participation unevenly; no clear position on this guarantee.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Part 2 rejects state ownership and bureaucratic rule in favour of worker partnership, so defending a bureaucratic planned state is not its position.

indirect-election.rationale: The Jamahiriya filled the General People's Congress with delegates from lower-level people's congresses and committees, though Part 1 criticises representation in parliaments.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from the Jamahiriya's practice of treating Islam as the state's religion and law; the Green Book does not discuss church status.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Part 3 makes the nation the unit of history and the Jamahiriya denied Amazigh recognition and autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Part 1 rejects referendums as a false form of democracy, but nothing addresses disputed territories; inferred as split.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from Gaddafi's pan-Arab and pan-African aims and his view of imperial borders as artificial; the Green Book does not state it.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from Part 2's idea that needs should be met but not exceeded and that wealth beyond needs is exploitative.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed; no clear position inferable.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from the Jamahiriya's practice of arming and training women in military academies and the people's-army ideal, though the Green Book does not state it.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The Green Book makes the nation and its social bond the driver of history and stresses attachment to land and tribe; the duty to protect ancestral land is inferred.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Not addressed in the Green Book; inferred from its stress on popular law and custom, against which killing without trial sits poorly, though the Jamahiriya practised repression.

close-ties-china.rationale: The Jamahiriya's foreign policy was anti-imperialist and shifted over time; no clear line on China is in the sources.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The Green Book treats the nation as a social bond of shared origin, and Gaddafi backed Arab and African causes; protecting kin in neighbouring states is inferred.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The Green Book holds land is no one's property and may be used only to meet one's own needs; the compensation idea is inferred.

self-ownership.rationale: The Green Book wants personal freedom, yet bars hiring labour and renting; adherents' answer is mixed and inferred.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The Green Book abolishes wages, profit and rent and has needs met directly; abolishing consumption taxes is inferred from that.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The Green Book wants basic needs of every person met by society, which leans universal; inferred.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The Green Book rejects parties and parliaments as barriers between people and power, but puts power in people's congresses rather than a leader; the leader wording makes this low.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The Green Book rejects profit and private business exploitation; special privileges for the connected are inferred to be rejected.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The Green Book bases law on custom and religion and does not discuss denominational party politics, which it rejects as parties anyway; adherents unclear.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Not addressed directly; the Green Book mixes industrial modernity with tradition and religion, but no explicit synthesis is stated.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Part 3 holds that men and women have different natural roles; the divorce question itself is inferred.

national-resource-control.rationale: The Jamahiriya nationalised oil and foreign firms and the Green Book rejects exploitation by outsiders and hired labour.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Part 2 ties just possession to need and labour rather than to how holdings were acquired, so a large unequal holding is illegitimate whatever the process.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its hostility to capitalism, profit and finance and its state-run trade.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Not addressed as stated; inferred from Part 3's view that historically oppressed groups are rising and that racial and national bonds shape history.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Not stated as such; inferred from Part 1's claim that law must rest on custom and religion rather than on man-made procedure.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Not addressed; Part 2 wants workers as partners rather than wage earners, but says nothing on automation.

multipolar-world.rationale: The doctrine is offered as a third way outside both capitalist and Marxist blocs, with anti-imperialist foreign policy.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Part 2 holds that workers are entitled to what they produce and rejects wages, profit and rent as exploitation of labour.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Part 3 makes the national and social bond the driver of history and pairs it with worker partnership and anti-imperialism.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred: it puts nation and social bond ahead of class, not a left-wing material-first programme.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: It abolishes parties, profit and wage labour, so a party-led market economy contradicts its core.

missingStatements.text: Political parties and parliaments should be abolished so that the people rule directly through local assemblies.
missingStatements.rationale: The Green Book calls parliament a misrepresentation and parties a form of dictatorship.

missingStatements.text: No one should be allowed to rent out housing; every family should own the home it lives in.
missingStatements.rationale: Part 2 says renting housing, even from the state, compromises freedom, and the regime turned tenants into owners.

missingStatements.text: A professional army should be replaced by an armed citizenry.
missingStatements.rationale: The motto puts weapons in the hands of the people, as part of popular authority.

notes: Practice diverged sharply from theory: Gaddafi held great power without formal office, and the regime banned parties and repressed dissent. Answers follow the stated theory unless marked otherwise.
